Add to the Makefile or a `scripts/test_hook_chain.sh`:
```
# Install stub Gerrit hook
echo '#!/bin/sh\necho "Change-Id: Ideadbeef">>"$1"' > .git/hooks/commit-msg.legacy && chmod +x .git/hooks/commit-msg.legacy
# Run checker against a conforming message

```

findings.finding: The carve-out for 'lines whose length comes from one unsplittable atomic token (URL/path/dotted identifier)' in AC4 does not specify the detection rule an executor must implement. Three plausible interpretations exist: (a) the token alone is longer than 72 chars, (b) removing the token makes the remainder ≤72 chars, or (c) the line consists solely of the token plus optional whitespace/punctuation. An executor must invent this rule, risking divergent implementations.

findings.finding: The plan defines no RETIRE/cleanup path for `commit-msg.legacy`. Pre-commit's `uninstall` command removes `.git/hooks/commit-msg` but does NOT restore the original hook from `.legacy`. After `pre-commit uninstall --hook-type commit-msg` (or a manual removal of the hook file), Gerrit's Change-Id hook is silently orphaned in `.legacy` and never runs — every subsequent commit is pushed without a Change-Id, breaking Gerrit integration with no warning.
findings.location: Critical risk handled: Gerrit's commit-msg hook / AC: `make hooks` prints a WARNING when no Change-Id stamping is found
scenarios: A developer who temporarily disables pre-commit (`pre-commit uninstall --hook-type commit-msg` or `rm .git/hooks/commit-msg`) will silently lose Change-Id stamping: `.legacy` exists but nothing calls it, so every `git push` to Gerrit is rejected server-side with 'missing Change-Id'.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to CONTRIBUTING.md (and optionally a `make unhooks` target): 'To remove the pre-commit gate, run `pre-commit uninstall --hook-type commit-msg` AND then `cp .git/hooks/commit-msg.legacy .git/hooks/commit-msg && chmod +x .git/hooks/commit-msg` to restore Gerrit's Change-Id hook.' Also have `make hooks` detect and warn if `.legacy` is present but `commit-msg` is NOT a pre-commit-managed file (indicating a prior partial uninstall).
